content: Take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are instructed to take it three times a week, space the doses at least 48 hours apart and take them on the same days each week (e.g., Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays) at the same time of day. Continue taking this medication, along with any other tuberculosis (TB) medications, for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, joint pain, and headache. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Bedaquiline may cause a rash, which is usually not serious, but it can be difficult to distinguish from a rare rash that may indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before starting bedaquiline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Bedaquiline may affect the heart rhythm, potentially causing a condition called QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause this condition. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are using diuretics (water pills) or experiencing severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication, as it may increase the risk of liver disease. Bedaquiline may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly needed. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect how bedaquiline is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., liver function tests, EKG, potassium, calcium, and magnesium levels) should be performed before starting this medication and periodically during treatment. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a daily dose during the first two weeks of treatment, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. If you miss a dose from week three onward, take it as soon as you remember, then return to your usual three-times-a-week dosing schedule. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. If you are using the 20-milligram tablets, keep the drying agent (desiccant) in the bottle. If necessary, the 100-milligram tablets may be stored in another container for up to three months. Always tightly close the bottle when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
